# Psalm 150 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Praise Yah! Praise God in-his-sanctuary; praise-him in-firmament-of his-strength.

**2** Praise-him for-his-mighty-deeds; praise-him according-to-abundance-of his-greatness.

**3** Praise-him with-blast-of the-horn; praise-him with-harp and-lyre.

**4** Praise-him with-tambourine and-dance; praise-him with-strings and-pipe.

**5** Praise-him with-cymbals-of sound; praise-him with-cymbals-of shouting.

**6** All the-breath let-it-praise Yah! Praise Yah!

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **150:1-6**: The grand finale of the Psalter. Six verses, thirteen 'praises' — the entire book resolves into pure, unrestricted praise. Every instrument, every location, every breath.

- **150:6**: 'All the-breath' (kol hanneshamah) — the final word of the Psalter summons every breathing creature to praise. The book that began with 'Blessed' (1:1) ends with 'Praise Yah.'

— EMET
